checks.name: A3-reclaim-skip-branches
checks.summary: Three subtests, one per skip branch, all PASS: TestClaimReclaimSkipsWhenSupersededExecutionIsAbsent (the expired Lease's ExecutionID has no saved Execution, manufactured directly against the store since Service.Claim itself never produces this), TestClaimReclaimSkipsWhenSupersededExecutionAlreadyTerminal (the superseded Execution already reached ExecutionSucceeded via the ordinary happy path before its Lease's TTL elapsed), and TestClaimReclaimSkipsWhenSupersededExecutionLinkageMismatches (the superseded Execution's FencingToken was corrupted directly against the store so it no longer matches its own Lease). In every case Claim still succeeded and returned a usable new Lease/Execution, and the superseded Execution was left byte-for-byte unchanged. The already-terminal and linkage-mismatch tests each also prove the negative direction: an unconditional domain.MarkExecutionLost call on the exact same Execution/Lease pair (what Claim would do without the guard) fails with domain.ErrInvalidTransition and domain.ErrStaleFence respectively -- the exact errors an unconditional call would have propagated out of Claim, which is why the guard exists (dp-v2-058 d5).

checks.name: A14-make-check-post-commit
checks.summary: Second make check run: environment/format/lint/test/contracts/docs all pass, and ownership/component-store-firestore/workflow-pins were separately confirmed green, but the secrets step (gitleaks git --no-banner --redact) fails. Root cause, isolated with `gitleaks git --log-opts="5bceb5f..HEAD"` (5bceb5f is this task's base commit): exactly 2 findings, both generic-api-key false positives on commit e1c46da (this task's first evidence commit) -- its check summaries restated the raw evidence_key hash values in prose followed by a period, which falls outside .gitleaks.toml's existing anchored allowlist for 64-hex values in .agents/v2/ (the allowlist requires the captured match to equal ^[a-f0-9]{64}$ exactly; a trailing period breaks that match). This was corrected in the immediately following commit (the raw hashes no longer appear anywhere outside their JSON evidence_key fields), but commit e1c46da's own historical diff still contains the original text and is permanently part of local branch history: gitleaks git with no --log-opts scans full history, so it re-flags that commit's diff on every run regardless of later fixes. Fixing this fully requires rewriting commit e1c46da (e.g. squash or amend), which is outside this task's permitted git operations (git reset / git checkout -- / git stash / --amend are prohibited by the work order). The full, unscoped `make check` run also separately surfaces 2 more generic-api-key findings on commit ae9a178, which is on branch v2-task/V2-045 (not an ancestor of this task's base or branch, confirmed with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`), committed by a concurrent agent in a sibling worktree sharing this repository's object store literally seconds before this check ran -- unrelated to V2-058, outside internal/application and internal/runner, and not fixable from this task. This is recorded as failed, not passed or skipped, because it was actually executed and did not succeed; see the staleness/escalation note for the recommended resolution (squash-merge or an authorised history rewrite of e1c46da).

Until one of these happens, `make check`'s secrets step on this branch, scanned in isolation from other branches (`git log --log-opts="5bceb5f..HEAD"`), remains red for this reason alone; scanned unscoped (as the Makefile invokes it), it is additionally, and independently, red because of the unrelated v2-task/V2-045 commit, which is not this task's defect to fix.
